items.title: 3.1.1 Analyzing Quadratic Function by Sketching (Roman Urdu)

blocks.text: Pichle page par hum ne quadratic function ki shakal \(f(x) = ax^{2} + bx + c\) dekhi. Ab sawal yeh hai ke is ka graph kaisa dikhta hai, aur graph dekh kar hum function ke baare mein kya kya bata sakte hain. Is sabaq ke baad aap kisi bhi quadratic function ka sketch khud bana sakenge aur us ki choti (ya tah) aur barhne ghatne wale hisse pehchaan sakenge.

Jaisa ke hum jaante hain, quadratic function \(f(x) = ax^{2} + bx + c\) ke graph ki shakal parabola hoti hai. Parabola upar ki taraf khulta hai ya neeche ki taraf, yeh leading coefficient \(a\) ke sign par munhasir hai, jaisa ke figure mein dikhaya gaya hai.

blocks.alt: Two parabolas side by side. Left, a greater than 0: the curve opens upward and the vertex V is its lowest point. Right, a less than 0: the curve opens downward and the vertex V is its highest point. A dashed vertical line through V in each is the axis of symmetry.
blocks.caption: Figure: a parabola opens upward when a > 0 and downward when a < 0; V is the vertex (original drawing after the textbook's figure)

blocks.text: Parabola ki nok (tip), jise upar diagrams mein \(V\) likha hai, vertex kehlati hai aur is ke coordinates \((h, k)\) hain. Vertex se guzarne wali khari (vertical) line parabola ki axis of symmetry (tanazur ki lakeer) hai. Vertex ek turning point (morne ki jagah) hai, jahan graph apni simt badalta hai.

items: Agar \(a > 0\) ho to vertex minimum point (sab se neecha point) hai.
Agar \(a < 0\) ho to vertex maximum point (sab se ooncha point) hai.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
\(a\) ka sign shakal kyun tay karta hai? Jab \(x\) bohat bara ho (positive ya negative), to \(ax^{2}\) wala term \(bx + c\) se kahin zyada bara ho jata hai. Misaal: \(x = 100\) par \(x^{2} = 10000\), jab ke \(x\) sirf 100 hai. Is liye graph ke dono kinaron par asal hukumat \(ax^{2}\) ki hoti hai. Agar \(a > 0\) ho to dono kinaron par \(ax^{2}\) bara aur positive hai, yani dono baazu (arms) upar jate hain: curve upar khulta hai aur us ka ek sab se neecha point hota hai. Agar \(a < 0\) ho to dono baazu neeche jate hain aur curve ka ek sab se ooncha point hota hai.
Ek aasan tareeqa yaad rakhne ka: \(a > 0\) ho to parabola "muskurata chehra" (smile) hai, aur \(a < 0\) ho to "udaas chehra".
"Axis of symmetry" ka matlab yeh hai ke agar graph ko line \(x = h\) par kaghaz ki tarah tehh (fold) karein to dono hisse bilkul ek doosre par aa jayenge. Isi liye vertex hamesha do \(x\)-intercepts ke bilkul beech mein hota hai (jab woh mojood hon).

Quadratic function ka sketch banane ke liye humein \(x\)-intercept, \(y\)-intercept aur vertex maloom karne hote hain. Aur sketch ka tajziya (analysis) karne ke liye hum dekhte hain ke vertex minimum point hai ya maximum, aur woh intervals batate hain jahan function increasing (barh raha) ya decreasing (ghat raha) hai.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Sketch banane ka qadam ba qadam tareeqa (yeh hamari taraf se hai, ise apni copy mein likh lijiye):
1. \(y\)-intercept: \(x = 0\) rakhein; yeh hamesha \((0, c)\) hota hai.
2. \(x\)-intercepts: \(ax^{2} + bx + c = 0\) ko factorization ya quadratic formula se hal karein. Agar \(b^{2} - 4ac < 0\) ho to koi real root nahi, yani graph \(x\)-axis ko chhoota hi nahi.
3. Vertex: \(h = \frac{-b}{2a}\), \(k = f(h)\).
4. Shakal: \(a > 0\) to upar khulta hai (vertex minimum), \(a < 0\) to neeche khulta hai (vertex maximum).
5. Points lagayein aur ek hamwar (smooth) U shakal ka curve banayein jo \(x = h\) ke dono taraf ek jaisa ho.
Increasing ka matlab: \(x\) daen taraf barhe to \(y\) upar jaye. Decreasing ka matlab: \(x\) daen taraf barhe to \(y\) neeche aaye. Parabola mein yeh tabdeeli hamesha \(x = h\) par hoti hai.

blocks.title: Dhyan dein
blocks.text: Har parabola \(x\)-axis ko nahi kaatta. Misaal ke taur par \(y = x^{2} + 1\) ki sab se neechi value 1 hai, is liye yeh graph hamesha \(x\)-axis se upar rehta hai aur is ke koi \(x\)-intercepts nahi. Aisi soorat mein sirf \(y\)-intercept, vertex aur vertex ke dono taraf ek do mazeed points (jaise \(x = h \pm 1\)) le kar sketch banaiye. Aur yaad rakhiye: \(y\)-intercept har quadratic function ka hota hai, kyun ke \(x = 0\) hamesha rakha ja sakta hai.
Ab kitab ki misaal mein yeh saare qadam chala kar dekhte hain. Har step ke saath "Kyun" zaroor parhiye, taa ke aap ko sirf tareeqa nahi balke us ki wajah bhi samajh aaye.

blocks.title: Example 1
steps:
Given: \(y = -x^{2} - 2x + 3\), yani \(a = -1\), \(b = -2\), \(c = 3\).
To find: \(y\)-intercept, \(x\)-intercepts aur vertex; phir sketch, vertex maximum point hai ya minimum, aur function kahan barhta (increasing) aur kahan ghatta (decreasing) hai.
Method: sab se pehle hum dekhte hain ke parabola ko banane ke liye kya chahiye. Teen khaas points kaafi hain: \(y\)-intercept ke liye \(x = 0\) rakhein, \(x\)-intercepts ke liye \(y = 0\) wali equation hal karein, aur vertex ke liye \(h = \frac{-b}{2a}\) aur \(k = y(h)\). In points ko jor kar graph ban jata hai.

Step 1: \(y\)-intercept
\[y = -(0)^{2} - 2(0) + 3\]
\[y = 3\]
Kyun: \(y\)-axis par har point ka \(x\) zero hota hai. Is liye graph \(y\)-axis ko \((0, 3)\) par kaatta hai. Ek aasan baat yaad rakhiye: har quadratic function ka \(y\)-intercept seedha \(c\) hota hai, kyun ke \(x = 0\) rakhne se \(ax^{2}\) aur \(bx\) dono zero ho jate hain.

Step 2: \(x\)-intercepts: \(y = 0\) rakhein
\[-x^{2} - 2x + 3 = 0\]
\[x^{2} + 2x - 3 = 0\]
Kyun: \(x\)-axis par har point ka \(y\) zero hota hai, is liye \(y = 0\) wali equation ke roots hi \(x\)-intercepts hain. Phir hum ne dono taraf \(-1\) se multiply kiya taa ke \(x^{2}\) ka coefficient positive ho jaye. Is se factorization aasan hoti hai, aur roots par koi asar nahi parta, kyun ke \(0 \times (-1)\) bhi zero hi hai.

Step 3: Middle term tor kar factorize karein
\[x^{2} + 3x - x - 3 = 0\]
\[x(x + 3) - 1(x + 3) = 0\]
\[(x + 3)(x - 1) = 0\]
Kyun: humein do aise numbers chahiye jin ka product \(-3\) (yani \(a \times c\)) aur sum \(2\) (yani \(b\)) ho. Yeh \(3\) aur \(-1\) hain, kyun ke \(3 \times (-1) = -3\) aur \(3 + (-1) = 2\). Is liye \(2x\) ko \(3x - x\) likha.

Step 4: Har factor ko zero rakhein
\[x + 3 = 0 \;\text{ ya }\; x - 1 = 0\]
\[x = -3,\quad x = 1\]
Kyun: do cheezon ka product tabhi zero hota hai jab un mein se koi ek zero ho. Is liye graph \(x\)-axis ko \((-3, 0)\) aur \((1, 0)\) par kaatta hai.

Step 5: Vertex nikaalein
\[h = \dfrac{-b}{2a} = -\dfrac{(-2)}{2(-1)}\]
\[h = -1\]
\[k = -(-1)^{2} - 2(-1) + 3\]
\[k = -1 + 2 + 3 = 4\]
Kyun: vertex hamesha axis of symmetry \(x = h\) par hota hai, aur \(h = \frac{-b}{2a}\) hai (yeh formula kahan se aata hai, woh hum 3.1.2 mein dekhenge). \(k\) woh value hai jo \(y\) ko \(x = h\) par milti hai, is liye \(h\) ko function mein rakh diya.
Dhyan dein: \(-(-1)^{2} = -1\) hai, \(+1\) nahi. Pehle square hota hai (\((-1)^{2} = 1\)), phir bahar wala minus lagta hai. Yahan sab se zyada ghaltiyan hoti hain.

Step 6: Maximum ya minimum? Sketch banayein
Yahan \(a = -1 < 0\) hai, is liye parabola neeche ki taraf khulta hai aur vertex \((-1, 4)\) maximum point hai. Ab points \((-3, 0)\), \((1, 0)\), \((0, 3)\) aur \((-1, 4)\) graph par lagayein aur unhein ek hamwar (smooth) curve se jorein jo line \(x = -1\) ke dono taraf ek jaisa ho (neeche figure dekhiye).
Kyun: \(a < 0\) ho to curve apne sab se oonche point par mur jata hai. Is liye 4 se bari koi \(y\) value is function ki nahi ho sakti.

Step 7: Barhne aur ghatne ke intervals
\(x = -1\) ke baen (left) taraf curve upar ja raha hai; \(x = -1\) ke daen (right) taraf neeche aa raha hai. Is liye function \(y\) interval \((-\infty, -1)\) par increasing aur \((-1, \infty)\) par decreasing hai.
Kyun: graph ko hamesha baen se daen parhte hain. Jab \(x\) barhne ke saath \(y\) barhe to function increasing, aur jab \(x\) barhne ke saath \(y\) ghate to decreasing. Turning point (vertex) hi woh jagah hai jahan yeh rawayya badalta hai, is liye dono intervals \(-1\) par milte hain.

Tasdeeq:
Ab dekhte hain ke jawab sahi hai ya nahi. Dono \(x\)-intercepts axis se barabar door hone chahiye: \(\frac{-3 + 1}{2} = -1 = h\). Bilkul sahi.
Ek symmetric jora: \(y(-2) = -4 + 4 + 3 = 3\) aur \(y(0) = 3\); dono points \(x = -1\) se ek ek unit door hain aur values barabar hain.
Ek aur point: \(y(2) = -4 - 4 + 3 = -5\), jo 4 se chhota hai. Is liye vertex wali value 4 waqai sab se bari hai.
blocks.answer: \(y\)-intercept \(3\); \(x\)-intercepts \(-3\) aur \(1\); vertex \((-1, 4)\) maximum point hai (\(a < 0\)). Function \((-\infty, -1)\) par increasing aur \((-1, \infty)\) par decreasing hai.

blocks.alt: Graph of y = minus x squared minus 2x plus 3 on a grid from x = minus 4 to 2. The parabola opens downward, crosses the x-axis at minus 3 and 1, crosses the y-axis at 3, and has its highest point, the vertex, at (minus 1, 4). A dashed vertical line x = minus 1 is the axis of symmetry.
blocks.caption: Figure: y = −x² − 2x + 3 with vertex (−1, 4), x-intercepts −3 and 1, y-intercept 3 (original drawing after the textbook's figure)

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text:
Example 1 ke graph ko dekh kar batayein: function ki range kya hai? Yani \(y\) kaun kaun si values le sakta hai?
Jawab: sab se oonchi value 4 hai aur neeche ki taraf curve hamesha jata rehta hai, is liye range \((-\infty, 4]\) hai, yani \(y \le 4\). Yeh baat 3.1.2 aur Exercise 3.1 mein bohat kaam aayegi.

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
Yeh hamari practice hai, kitab ka sawal nahi: \(y = x^{2} - 4x + 3\) ko analyze karein.
\(y\)-intercept: \(x = 0\) par \(y = 3\).
\(x\)-intercepts: \(x^{2} - 4x + 3 = (x - 1)(x - 3) = 0\), is liye \(x = 1\) aur \(x = 3\).
Vertex: \(h = \frac{-(-4)}{2(1)} = 2\), \(k = 4 - 8 + 3 = -1\), yani \((2, -1)\).
\(a = 1 > 0\), is liye parabola upar khulta hai aur \((2, -1)\) minimum point hai.
Function \((-\infty, 2)\) par decreasing aur \((2, \infty)\) par increasing hai (Example 1 ka bilkul ulat, kyun ke yahan \(a\) positive hai).
Tasdeeq: \(\frac{1 + 3}{2} = 2 = h\). Sahi!

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. \(f(x) = ax^{2} + bx + c\) ka graph parabola hai.
2. \(a > 0\): upar khulta hai, vertex minimum point. \(a < 0\): neeche khulta hai, vertex maximum point.
3. Vertex \((h, k)\) turning point hai; axis of symmetry khari line \(x = h\) hai, jahan \(h = \frac{-b}{2a}\).
4. Sketch ke liye: \(y\)-intercept \((0, c)\), \(x\)-intercepts (\(f(x) = 0\) ke roots) aur vertex.
5. Function \(x = h\) par increasing se decreasing (ya ulat) mein badalta hai.
6. Dono \(x\)-intercepts ka average hamesha \(h\) hota hai; yeh ek aasan check hai.

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. Minus ke andar negative ka square: \(-(-1)^{2} = -1\) hai, \(+1\) nahi. Bachne ka tareeqa: pehle bracket ka square likhein, phir bahar ka sign lagayein.
2. Intercepts ulat dena: \(y\)-intercept \(x = 0\) se aata hai, aur \(x\)-intercepts \(y = 0\) se.
3. Intervals ulte likhna: graph ko hamesha baen se daen parhein. \(a < 0\) ho to pehle increasing phir decreasing; \(a > 0\) ho to pehle decreasing phir increasing.
4. Vertex par nokdaar (V jaisa) kona bana dena: parabola vertex par gol aur hamwar hota hai.
5. \(h = \frac{-b}{2a}\) mein \(b\) ka sign bhool jana: \(b = -2\) ho to \(-b = +2\).
